look_here_first: Look at the architecture: a tall plant with long bare internodes and an open candelabra-like panicle made of many short compact flower spikes; the leaves are simple, narrow, sharply serrate, and not lobed.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: introduced South American annual or short-lived perennial, often 0.9–2.3 m tall

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: erect strongly 4-sided green stems with long internodes

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: opposite simple elliptic to oblanceolate leaves, sharply serrate above midblade

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaves sessile/subsessile and not deeply lobed

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: open panicle with several orders of opposite branching

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: many short compact terminal spikelets rather than a few long spikes

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: tiny violet-purple flowers and prolific small mericarps/seeds

key_traits.label: Verbena training
key_traits.text: Tall open candelabra architecture + simple narrow serrate leaves + many short compact spikes separates this common invasive from local native Verbena.
